To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the patient, physician, and system level factors are important in determining the quality of care of patients with type 2 diabetes in primary care.

the management of type II diabetes mellitus is influenced by a number of factors, both patient and physician, and that the management of the condition is influenced by the type of health insurance the patient has.

the patient, physician and system factors are all important in the management of diabetes and that these factors can be addressed by the development and implementation of a multifactorial intervention.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the patient in the management of diabetes.
the role of patient, doctor and systemic factors in determining how people manage their type 2 diabetes.
the role of patient, provider and system factors in the management and outcomes of patients with diabetes mellitus.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the patient, the physician, and the system in which care is provided all have a significant impact on the care of the patient with type 2 diabetes.

there is a need for a more integrated and holistic approach to type 2 diabetes management that includes patient and physician factors, as well as the role of the health system in the overall management and treatment of the disease.
there are a number of factors, both patient, physician and system related that influence the management of type II diabetes mellitus.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the management of type two diabetes mellitus (T2DM) in the United Kingdom is suboptimal and requires improvement.
the patient, physician and system all contribute to the management of type II diabetes mellitus and the quality of care.
we have identified several patient, physician, and health care system factors that may contribute to the underutilization of recommended care for type 2 diabetes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
patients with type 2 diabetes have a high prevalence of anxiety symptoms and that this may impact on their diabetes self-management.
there is no one-size-fits-all approach to treating diabetes.
the majority of patients with diabetes are not achieving recommended blood pressure goals.
